heading: 4.8 Exploratory Objective Eight: abdominal ultrasound
objective: To explore the diagnostic performance and supported clinical and recorded-cost context of abdominal ultrasound alone and with MAS, compared with the established MAS–hs-CRP strategies.
methods: The recorded abdominal-scan variable (abd_SCAN) was checked in both available SPSS files. Code 1 denotes acute appendicitis, code 2 other diagnosis, code 3 normal study/inconclusive, code 4 appendiceal mass, code 5 inconclusive and code 6 not done. Appendiceal inflammatory mass can accompany complicated appendicitis. A mass explicitly reported as consistent with appendicitis is therefore test-positive. For this analysis, the single code 4 record is conditionally treated as an appendicitis-related positive finding.
finalParagraph: The analysis recognises appendiceal mass as a positive ultrasound finding when consistent with appendicitis, rather than treating it as evidence against disease. In the 67-record conditional analysis, ultrasound sensitivity is 87.7% and accuracy 85.1%. The original report is needed to confirm the single mass classification; indeterminate scans remain excluded and missing results remain separate. The small reference-negative group limits precision, and neither incremental costs nor ultrasound-specific confidence effects can be estimated.
